subtitulo: Repair one noisy transport exchange without switching to English
introPt: A bus-counter answer arrives too fast. Listen to the traveller climb only as far as necessary: signal the break, slow it down, then write the departure time.
cenario: At a busy bus counter, the traveller needs the departure time and the correct entrance.

dialogo.es: Sale a las quince cincuenta por la entrada del fondo.
dialogo.pinyin: SAH-leh ah lahs KEEN-seh seen-KWEN-tah por lah en-TRAH-dah del FOHN-doh
dialogo.pt: It leaves at 15:50 through the entrance at the back.

dialogo.es: No entendí. ¿Me lo puede repetir más despacio?
dialogo.pinyin: noh en-ten-DEE. meh loh PWEH-deh reh-peh-TEER mahs dehs-PAH-syoh
dialogo.pt: I didn't understand. Can you repeat that more slowly?

dialogo.es: Claro. Sale a las quince cincuenta.
dialogo.pinyin: KLAH-roh. SAH-leh ah lahs KEEN-seh seen-KWEN-tah
meh loh PWEH-deh ehs-kree-BEER, por fah-BOR
dialogo.pt: Can you write it down for me, please?

perguntas.explica: The traveller states the break instead of pretending to understand.

opcoes: To reduce speed while keeping the exchange spoken
perguntas.explica: The second rung keeps the information in the ear but makes it more recoverable.

perguntas.pergunta: Why move the time into writing?
opcoes: The attendant asked for a signature
Quince and cincuenta remain fragile in the ear
perguntas.explica: Numbers are high-cost payloads; writing gives both people the same value to verify.

perguntas.pergunta: What time does the bus leave?
perguntas.explica: The written payload is quince cincuenta: 15:50.

perguntas.pergunta: When should the traveller use the map rung?
opcoes: When a written route still does not identify where to move
perguntas.explica: The map externalises spatial information after words and writing have reached their limit.
